decisions.executionNote: Start continuous elbow-up approach with both grippers open, pitching toward a top-down grasp; estimate object heights and tool offset from updated RGB.
Retry with half-size pitch and translation increments to respect the initial IK continuity guard.
Approach yellow car with left arm and white car with right arm, completing downward tool orientation above the table.
Lower cautiously toward both cars and refine centering using wrist views before closing.
Center right gripper slightly left, close around both cars, and test retention with a short vertical lift.
Lift vertically with closed commands to verify both car grasps visually before transporting.
Neither car retained in RGB. Reopen and descend farther, accounting for their small shifts, to grasp below the upper surfaces.
Close at the lower car grasp level and perform a small vertical retention test without lateral motion.
Raise for clear visual confirmation; left car appears between jaws but right retention is uncertain.
Recenter on current car positions and approach a deeper side grasp; previous lifts showed both cars still on the table.
Table contact limits further descent. Relieve contact, restore downward orientation and adjust cars deeper between the finger pads using wrist centering.
Account for forward offset of the finger pads, moving the cars farther between them before closing at the safe table height.
Verify the offset-adjusted grasp with a vertical lift; retention remains uncertain from the occluded wrist views.
Reopen and correct the forward overshoot, aligning at car centers while stopping above the observed table-contact limit.
Fine-center the cars in the open jaws at the safe grasp height, then close without lifting.
Lift both cars vertically while maintaining closed targets, checking for retention before basket travel.
Left car is retained: transport toward the middle basket. Right car was not retained: reopen and yaw to grasp across its width.
Use a lower, shorter-step path toward the blue basket after the left IK guard. Complete the right car's width-aligned grasp.
Move the held left car over the near interior of the middle basket with conservative extension; vertically test the newly aligned right grasp.
Retract the left wrist and tilt its held car forward over the basket, preserving elbow-up margin instead of extending farther. Continue right retention lift.
Reduce the initial left retraction/tilt increments after continuity rejection, then gradually restore margin; maintain closed car grasps.
Release the retained yellow car well inside the middle basket. Reapproach the white car with its long axis aligned between the jaws and level downward fingers.
Yellow car is in the blue basket. Withdraw the left arm toward the silver watch; center and close the right gripper lower around the white car.
Approach the silver watch at safe table height while checking the white car's new grip with a straight lift.
White car is visibly retained. Carry it toward the middle basket using forward tilt for reach margin; center and close around the silver watch and test lift.
Carry the silver watch toward the left basket and the retained white car toward the middle basket, keeping arms on their respective sides and tilted for reach margin.
Place the white car farther inside the blue basket and release. Silver watch slipped back onto the table; return the left open gripper to regrasp.
Both cars are in the middle basket. Lower around the silver watch closer to the table; move the right open arm toward the second watch without crossing sides.
Allow the silver-watch closure to settle before a small lift; lower the right open gripper around the black watch.
Carry the retained silver watch over the left basket with forward tilt. Close around the black watch and make a short retention lift.
Release the silver watch into the left basket. Reapproach the displaced black watch slightly lower and farther back; prepare the left arm near the red chocolate bar.
Align the left gripper across the red bar's narrow width and lower. Let the black-watch grip settle, then lift to verify retention.
Refine red-bar centering between the pads. Reopen and regrasp the black watch farther back at the table-safe depth; prior right lift was empty.
Let both grasps settle, then lift vertically to confirm the red bar and black watch are retained.
Both objects are retained. Move them to separated central staging points for table-mediated transfers, keeping wrists on their own sides and avoiding arm crossing.
Set the red bar down at the central transfer area. The black watch slipped during transport; reopen and return to its visible landing position on the right.
Clear the left arm away from the staged bar. Center the right fingers around the watch at table height and close slowly before another lift.
Gently lift the black watch without lateral acceleration. Reorient the waiting left gripper for receiving the watch at the center.
Regrasp the black watch slightly deeper with leveled fingers, targeting its solid body rather than the thin slipping bracelet.
Relieve slight table contact while centering over the watch body; allow closure to settle and test with a very short lift.
The watch appears clamped around its body. Lift and translate gently toward central staging, keeping a closed target and checking for slippage.
Gently lower the retained watch at the central transfer area with a slight inward tool tilt, leaving the right wrist on its own side.
Release the watch at center, clear the right arm toward the white chocolate bar, then approach the staged watch from the left without crossing wrists.
Continue the separated approach from the interrupted observation with smaller right yaw and translation increments.
Lower the left fingers around the staged watch while keeping the wrist left of center; align the right gripper across the white chocolate bar.
Close and test the transferred watch. Refine the white bar's width alignment and pad centering, then close at the safe table height.
Level the left pads to regrasp the slipped central watch, keeping the wrist left of center. Lift the white bar to verify its retention.
Close around the leveled watch and test a short lift. Reposition the right pads toward the white bar's middle, correcting the prior end-only grasp.
Close and lift the now-centered white bar. Regrasp the central watch slightly farther back to avoid pushing its solid face out of the finger pads.
Lift the clamped watch toward the left workspace. Retry the thin white bar at a slightly lower pad height before transporting it.
Carry the retained watch toward the left basket with reach-preserving tilt. Lift the white bar vertically to verify the lower grasp.
Both small objects slipped. Reopen and return to their current locations; regrasp lower and avoid rotating the watch during its next transport.
Center both objects precisely at the low finger-pad level and close while stationary; use no orientation changes during the next lift.
Lift vertically with fixed orientations and closed targets to verify both centered grasps before lateral transport.
Both objects are visibly retained. Transport gently toward their own-side baskets with fixed orientations to avoid the previous rotational slippage.
Use small guarded advances over the near basket interiors, then release the watch into the left basket and white bar into the right basket.
The watches and white bar are now in their assigned baskets. Withdraw both arms; use the left arm to reposition the remaining red bar for a clean right-side pickup.
Begin withdrawal with smaller increments to satisfy the continuity guard, then approach the remaining red bar with the left open gripper.
Continue the replan from the executed prefix with reduced left yaw increments; approach the red bar while clearing the right arm.
Relieve apparent left-basket rim contact: raise vertically first, then withdraw toward the table before any further sideways approach.
Clear the left arm toward its home side. Approach the staged red bar with the right wrist kept right of center and an inward tool tilt for the transfer grasp.
Increase the right tool's inward tilt to center on the staged bar while lowering; begin a continuous elbow-up return of the left arm toward origin.
Fine-align and close on the red bar at the low pad level while finishing the left arm's smooth return toward its initial pose.
Test red-bar retention with a vertical lift and unchanged right orientation; settle the left arm at its original open-gripper pose.
The tilted grasp was too shallow and the bar remained on the table. Reopen, recenter, and lower farther to account for the tilted tool's shorter vertical reach.
Relieve slight table contact, allow the red-bar closure to settle, and test a short lift without changing orientation.
The red bar is visibly retained. Carry it toward the right basket with fixed orientation and a closed target, leaving the left arm at origin.
Raise the retained bar slightly for rim clearance, then advance it over the right basket's interior without rotating the grasp.
Release the last red bar inside the right basket, then withdraw the right arm clear of the rim before returning to origin.
Both bars are now visible in the right basket. Retract and unwind the right wrist through the elbow-up configuration, keeping both grippers open.
Continue the right arm's smooth elbow-up reset, retracting and pitching toward its original open-gripper pose.
Finish the right arm's continuous return to the initial pose and correct the left arm's small residual, with both grippers open.
